questions: Can you confirm your current list of medications, including any changes or discontinuations in the past year, and any new allergies or reactions since your last medical review?

events.value: blood pressure drop to eighty over fifty

preop_note_claims: Patient's medical history includes Obesity (BMI 32), Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, and Hypertension.

Current medications include Metformin 500 mg twice daily, Lisinopril 10 mg once daily, and Atorvastatin 20 mg once daily; Ranitidine 150 mg twice daily was stopped 6 months ago due to resolution of GERD symptoms, and the patient now uses Omeprazole 20mg once daily for acid reflux.
Patient has a documented allergy to Penicillin (manifested as a rash).
ASA-PS classification is 3 due to the presence of controlled but significant comorbidities (Obesity, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension).
Airway assessment indicates no anticipated difficulties; plan for General Anesthesia with Ultrasound-Guided Regional Anesthesia (TAP Block) for post-operative pain management.
handoff_claims: Patient underwent elective Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy under General Anesthesia with Ultrasound-Guided TAP Block for post-operative pain management.

Anticipated issues include monitoring for pain control efficacy from the TAP block and managing potential side effects from anesthesia in the context of patient's comorbidities (Obesity, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension).
Key history to convey includes Penicillin allergy (rash), current medications (Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, Omeprazole), and the reason for stopping Ranitidine (resolution of GERD symptoms).
distractors: Fractured right wrist 15 years ago, fully healed
